the effects of the cholesterol synthesis inhibitors lovastatin (LVS), simvastatin (SMV), and mevastatin (MVS) on the subcellular localization of 3-hydroxymethylglutarate-coenzyme A (HMG-CoA) reductase, the rate-limiting step in cholesterol synthesis, using immunoelectron microscopy of frozen ultrathin liver sections from rats treated with the drugs.
the mechanism of the induction of HMG-Co-A reductase and the effects of the drug on the structure and functions of the liver.

lovastatin, an antihyperlipidemic drug, induces HMG-CoA-reductase directly on the membranes of the expanded smooth endoplamic reticulum in hepatocytes.

the SER whorls induced by lovastatin in hepatocytes represent the expanded smooth ER that contains the enzyme HMG-CoA Reductase, the rate limiting enzyme in cholesterol synthesis.
